title: The Emperor's Rare Seven-Day Horse (ES)
summary: Akbar challenges Birbal to find a rare horse that is neither black, white, brown, nor grey. Birbal finds the horse with an ingenious calendar condition.
full_text:
One afternoon, while inspecting the imperial stables, Emperor Akbar decided to test Birbal with an impossible request. In a teasing tone, the Emperor commanded:

'Birbal, I have heard travelers speak of a rare breed of horse that is neither black, nor white, nor brown, nor grey, nor roan, nor chestnut, nor piebald! I want you to scour Hindustan and bring me such a horse within one month, or admit that your wisdom cannot satisfy your Emperor!'

The courtiers snickered, knowing that every horse on earth possessed one of those common coat colors. Birbal had been trapped!

Birbal bowed serenely: 'Your Majesty's wish is my command. I shall depart on a journey to find this marvelous steed.'

Birbal took a month's leave and spent the time resting in his country estate.

On the thirtieth day, Birbal walked into the Diwan-i-Khas. Akbar leaned forward with a mischievous smile: 'Well, Birbal? Have you brought my rare horse, or do you confess defeat?'

Birbal bowed low: 'Sire, after traveling through distant mountains, I have found the exact horse you desired! Its coat is a wondrous, celestial color—neither black, nor white, nor brown, nor grey, nor any ordinary shade!'

Akbar was astonished: 'Truly? Where is it? Bring it before me at once!'

Birbal replied with absolute seriousness:

'Sire, the owner of the horse is a very eccentric sage. He agreed to surrender the magnificent beast on two strict conditions.

'First, Your Majesty must send a trusted groom to inspect and fetch the horse in person.

'And second, Your Majesty must send the groom on any day of the week—except Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, or Saturday! On any other day of the week, the horse may be collected!'

The entire court fell silent for a second, then erupted in uproarious laughter!

Akbar laughed until his royal crown tilted on his brow: 'Birbal, you match my impossible horse with an impossible calendar! You have outwitted me once again!' Akbar rewarded Birbal with a purse of gold for his brilliant turn of wit.
